feedback.text: The cap being worn wasn't approved for this look — this SKU didn't have a headwear item selected, but the render still shows a black cap on the model. Please regenerate without it.
feedback.inferredError: The composed prompt introduced a black nylon baseball cap as a co-worn item even though assets_selected for this angle carries a null sku_id for the headwear category — i.e. no actual headwear product was ever resolved for this look. The generic accessory clause in styling.md was applied without checking whether an asset had actually been resolved for that category.
feedback.inferredFix: The prompt should only reference an accessory item (headwear included) when assets_selected has a resolved, non-null sku_id for that category; when sku_id is null, the category must be dropped from the composed prompt entirely.

candidate_0.detail: Add a conditional rule: 'Only render a headwear item if assets_selected contains a resolved, non-null sku_id for the headwear category; if sku_id is null, omit headwear entirely from the composed prompt.'
candidate_0.rationale: The rejected prompt states outright 'A black nylon baseball cap is worn on the head' with no conditioning, while assets_selected for this exact angle carries `{"category": "headwear", "sku_id": null}` — the guidance clause that generated this line has no asset-availability check, so it always injects a cap for this look regardless of whether one was actually resolved.

confidence.reasoning: Fixes the root mechanism (missing asset-availability gate) at the guidance-document level, so every future SKU with an unresolved headwear sku_id inherits the correct behavior, not just this one variant.

candidate_1.detail: Pass the per-category sku_id resolution state into pose_styling_writer's input alongside angle.md/styling.md/posing.md, and instruct it to skip any category whose sku_id is null when writing composite_direction.
candidate_1.rationale: Same fix, applied one step upstream at the LLM composition step instead of the source document, so the model never even considers unresolved categories when drafting the prompt.

confidence.reasoning: Resolves this specific case but leaves the unconditional clause in styling.md untouched, so any downstream consumer that still reads styling.md directly (outside pose_styling_writer) would reproduce the same bug.
